title: [SEC4] test_ikm_fd_pbkdf2_rejected name unclear
description:
tests/userspace/test_kdf.c:641-699 — test_ikm_fd_pbkdf2_rejected()

The test function name and internal logic don't clearly explain WHY PBKDF2 rejects ikm_fd. The comment should clarify: PBKDF2 passwords are sensitive user input that must come from write() only, not stored in persistent KEY fds. HKDF IKM is cryptographic material (not user passwords) and can be chained across KEY fds via ikm_fd. This distinction is important for security reasoning but gets lost in the current test structure.

Suggested fix: Either rename to clarify the reason (e.g., test_pbkdf2_ikm_fd_unsupported), or add a block comment explaining the design rule (passwords != stored key material).

This is a maintenance issue: future reviewers may not immediately understand why the check at src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c:1780 exists.
